Generator.ShakeTest.label1.Text:
This test allows you to check the reliability of your machine in performing rapid movements without position misalignments.
It is a fundamental test for fine-tuning of your engraver.

It work by engraving a small reference cross, than shaking your laser head with lot of rapid movement, and then going back to original position and tracing the cross again.

The test is completed successfully if the initial cross and the final cross match (overlap).
If your engraver is unable to complete this test successfully you will need to check:

1. That the machine does not slip on the table due to vibrations during work.
2. The table itself and the workpiece do not shake during the test, due to vibrations.
3. That the drive belts are tensioned correctly
4. The screws and nuts are correctly tightened
5. The laser carriage has no mechanical resistance during movement at some points of its travel
6. The electrical wires do not act as a hindrance to the movement and do not detach/move from their connectors during the movement.

If these conditions are met, but the machine is not able to perform this test successfully, you can try to slightly decrease the speed limits set in the "Grbl Configuration ($110-$111)" or maximum accelerations.

LaserLifeEdit.label7.Text:
Name: A brief quick name for you, just to identify this module quickly.

Brand: Please write the brand name of laser module. Usually it is the same of the machine, but not always.

Model: Sometime the same machine can mount different laser models. Please write the exact model of laser module (not the machine model).

Optical Power: The optical power of the laser module expressed in W (watt). Sometime expressed as "optical power" or "output power". If you have it expressed in mW (milliwatt) simply divide by 1000.

Most laser modules have a label with this information. If not, please refer to engraver specification in user manual or manifacturer website.
LaserUsage.label1.Text: LaserGRBL tracks the useful life of your lasers, to let you know how much each laser module has been used. If you have more than one machine or laser module you can add them with the "add" button. In this case LaserGRBL will ask you which laser you are using at the time of connection, so as to assign consumption to the right module each time.
LaserUsage.label2.Text: Please click on "edit" and fill in all the information related to your laser module.

LegalDisclaimer.LblNotToy.Text:
Laser engraver are not toys!
- Always take precautions to protect your eyesight
- Be aware of the risk of fire
- Be careful not to breathe the fumes
- Prevent access to children, animals and unauthorized personnel
- Never leave the machine unattended
- Refer to the engraver manual for use, safety and maintenance instructions

ResumeJobForm.LblBrief.Text:
LaserGRBL can start this job again from beginning or try to resume from last known position.
As it is not always possible to determine the best restart position we let you to take the final decision.
Last speed, power and laser state are recovered automatically.
ResumeJobForm.LblDetected.Text: LaserGRBL detected last job was not completed!
ResumeJobForm.RbSomeLines.Text: Resume some lines before the stop
RunFromPositionForm.LblBrief.Text:
This feature allow to run your job starting from a specific line, skipping any previous movement.
LaserGRBL compute the exact position and state and put the engraver in the correct state.
SaveOptionForm.label2.Text:
If you need to export the gcode to use it outside of LaserGRBL, for example with a stand-alone controller, maybe you will find it useful to be able to export the header/footer code and the code between each passes.

NOTE: If you export gcode to re-load inside LaserGRBL it is better to use quick export instead.
SettingsForm.LblFooter.Text:
LaserGRBL will enqueue this GCode at the end of any job.
Can be used to push back your engraver in a initial state like going back to zero position
or sending M9 to turn off fan etc.

Here you can use the same syntax of custom buttons.
SettingsForm.LblHeader.Text:
LaserGRBL will append this GCode before starting any job.
You can customize this code, for example adding M8 to turn on fan.

Here you can use the same syntax of custom buttons if you need to push some positioning
related to the specific job is going to be executed.
SettingsForm.LblPasses.Text:
When performing multiple passes LaserGRBL will push this GCode in the between of each passes.
Can be used to move Z down to perform deeper cuts.

Here you can use the same syntax of custom buttons.
SettingsForm.LblWarnOrturAC.Text:
Ortur User: Ortur Firmware (all version up to 137) has a bug on the machining resume that prevents properly using the auto-cooling function.
Please do not use Automatic Cooling with Ortur engraver until a new firmware is released.
SettingsForm.label1.Text:
LaserGRBL use power modulation through G-Code "S command" to produce grayscale tones.
Your laser must support TTL control connected to arduino PIN D11.
If not, please disable PWM support.
SettingsForm.label10.Text:
Without "Continuous Jog" when jog button is pressed LaserGRBL send Jog request with settled speed and movement; and the jog is fully executed to the final position.
If you enable "Continuous Jog" jogging is sent with mouse-down and aborted/interrupted on mouse-up, so you can do approximative positioning but in a very comfortable way.

NOTE: "Continuous Jog" only work with Grbl v1.1 or later, and require table size is correctily configured in Grbl Configuration (Menu "Grbl" -> "Grbl Configuration" $130, $131, $132)
SettingsForm.label11.Text: LaserGRBL is not designed to support Z axis, but if you have a 3axis hardware maybe you could find this option usefull.
SettingsForm.label12.Text:
Some laser diodes can heat-up to much if they run for a long time at the highest power. To prevent diode overheating and increase your laser lifetime you can add some automatic cooling-down cycles that insert some pause during engraivng process.
If Auto Cooling is enabled LaserGRBL will send automatic "feed hold" and "job resume" according with ON-OFF timing configuration.
SettingsForm.label13.Text:
Time ON: this is the maximum time that Laser will stay on during engraving process.
After this time LaserGRBL will send an automatic feed hold to cool down the laser.
SettingsForm.label2.Text: If enabled LaserGRBL send a soft-reset when the connection to grbl is opened.
SettingsForm.label20.Text: Time OFF: after this cooling time LaserGRBL will send a resume command to continue engraving job.
SettingsForm.label21.Text:
Warning: this feature will work only with grbl versions > v1.1 with "laser mode" enabled.
If you use auto-cooling with older grbl version (or with laser mode disabled) the laser will not turn off during pauses
and burns holes in your work!
SettingsForm.label22.Text:
The max resolution available in LaserGRBL is 20 lines/mm (about 500dpi) that is high enough for most user.
If you need higher resolution you can enable "HiRes" and remove this limit.  Be careful: LaserGRBL will need many more resources!
SettingsForm.label23.Text:
Here you can set another sound for success events, like when a job is finished.
Check to enable.
SettingsForm.label24.Text:
Here you can set another warning sound.
This usually fired on a bad GCode command, but your machine can continue operating.
Check to enable.
SettingsForm.label28.Text:
Here you can set an error sound for fatal errors.
This means, your job most likely stopped, and LaserGRBL can not continue the operation.
Check to enable.
SettingsForm.label3.Text:
Connection Protocol:
- UsbSerial: is the most common protocol. Should be used if your engraver is connected to USB or COM port.
- UsbSerial2: an alternative implementation of USB serial to bypass Microsoft SerialPort issues
- Telnet: if you have a WiFi-Telnet bridge. Communication is implemented like a simple telnet client-server.
- LaserWebESP8266: support WiFi connection via WebSocket. Compatible with LaserWeb-ESP8266 software.
SettingsForm.label32.Text:
Here you can set a sound for a successful connection.
Check to enable.
SettingsForm.label36.Text:
Here you can set a sound for disconnection.
Useful for some WiFi connections.
Check to enable.
SettingsForm.label39.Text:
By default LaserGRBL use G0 - rapid movement - to skip white parts of your jobs. This speed up the engraving process but it can result in inaccurate positioning with disappointing results. It is usually possible to improve the results by correctly setting the maximum acceleration and speed values ($ 120,121,122 and $ 110,111,112) in the grbl configuration.

If you disable this feature LaserGRBL will use G1 linear movement at the same job speed, with the result that all the engraving process is done at the same speed. This will slow down the process, but can drammatically improve the result where others approacs fails.
SettingsForm.label4.Text:
Streaming Mode: [Default Buffered]
- Buffered: optimize commands streaming filling up grbl receive buffer [recommended]
- Synchronous: wait for the execution of each command prior to send the very next command [slower but safer]
- RepeatOnError:  same as Synchronous but repeat commands if detect error [experimental]
SettingsForm.label40.Text:
LaserGRBL will warn you if you are going to create a job bigger then your engraver workspace.
Set this flag if you don't whant this safety control.
SettingsForm.label41.Text: With "click 'n jog" enabled a double-click on preview surface will jog to the click position.
SettingsForm.label42.Text:
If you have telegram search for @LaserGRBL bot
Obtain your personal code and write it here!
SettingsForm.label43.Text:
Starting from version 4.6.1 LaserGRBL uses a better approximation algorithm of bezier curves, capable of returning more accurate results.
Disable this option if you prefer to use the old algorithm.
SettingsForm.label44.Text: Don't notify if job time less then
SettingsForm.label46.Text:
In enabled LaserGRBL send a $I command and detect some information from the machine (i.e. the machine rx buffer size).
Please do not disable this feature.
SettingsForm.label47.Text:
This option will remove safety reminder countdown to remember to wear safety googles.
I suggest to not disable this countdown, this allow you to have a 5 second chance to check everything is ok.
SettingsForm.label49.Text: Use old-style LaserGRBL icons [Nostalgia mode: ON]
SettingsForm.label5.Text: By default LaserGRBL produces engraving lines in both travel directions of the laser head. Some tests have shown that this mode (which is faster) produces lower quality results. If the maximum marking quality is desired, activate this option.
SettingsForm.label50.Text:
Rendering Mode
- Auto: Let LaserGRBL choose the best configuration for you (prefers hardware acceleration).
- Hardware Acceleration: Use OpenGL with hardware acceleration (if supported)
- Software Rendering: Use OpenGL with software rendering (select this option if you have issues with hardware acceleration)
- Legacy: Disable OpenGL and use old preview form (select this option on old computer)
SettingsForm.label6.Text:
Threading Mode: UltraFast, Fast, Quiet, Slow. [Default Fast]
This setting affect the speed of sending thread and the frequency of status report request.
Set slower values if you are experiencing issues.
SettingsForm.label7.Text:
LaserGRBL can detect issues and warn the user providing info about how to solve them.
If disabled all the issues are silently managed without warning.
SettingsForm.label8.Text: If enabled LaserGRBL send a hard-reset when the connection to grbl is opened. [Position is lost!]
SettingsForm.label9.Text:
Firmware type
- Grbl: the awesome firmware for which LaserGRBL was developed for.
- Smoothie [experimental]: support has been added recently and is not fully tested.
- Marlin [experimental]: support has been added recently and is not fully tested.
- VigoWork [experimental]: support for VG-L7x model that is non grbl-standard.
